ordered_targets.name: Cubic ReDoS in queryPattern via \s* / [^: ]+ dual-backtracking on whitespace input
ordered_targets.mechanism: Characters matching both \s and [^: ] (e.g., tab 0x09) create nested backtracking: \s* at the regex prefix greedily consumes all tabs then backtracks O(n) times; at each backtrack position, [^"][^: ]+ in the name group greedily matches exposed tabs and backtracks O(n) times seeking a colon; find() repeats this at O(n) start positions. Total: O(n^3/6) regex backtracking steps.
ordered_targets.resource: CPU time: regex backtracking steps growing as n^3/6 with input length n
ordered_targets.scale: Measured CPU time: 11ms at 64B, 36ms at 128B, 81ms at 256B, 351ms at 512B, ≥2000ms (capped) at 1024B. Doubling ratios accelerate from 3.2× to ≥5.7×, consistent with O(n^3/6) cubic growth where lower-order terms depress ratios at small n. Conservative extrapolation using exponent 2.5 from n=1024 (≥2000ms): timeout (20s) at ~2560 tab bytes; at n=10240: ~1.2 million ms. Tab 0x09 is the densest encoding: one byte per unit of the parameter (input length), with each tab matching both \s* and [^: ]+ to drive the dual-backtracking cubic mechanism.
